items.title: $10,000 in Tesla When It Joined the S&P 500 Would Be About $15,700 Today. An Index Fund Would Have Done Better.
items.summary: Tesla stock purchased at $695 when it joined the S&P 500 in December 2020 has returned 57% over nearly six years, translating to roughly 8% annually. Despite the company tripling its revenue and achieving profitability, most of its growth was already priced into the initial valuation, causing the stock's P/E ratio to compress from 900x to 330x earnings.

The company's Google Search dominance (90%+ market share) generates $81 billion in ad revenue, while its Google Cloud AI business is experiencing explosive growth.

items.title: ExxonMobil Has Raised Its Dividend 43 Years Running. Here's the One Year the Streak Almost Broke.

The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $3.9-$4.2 billion with expected 34% gross margins, though it trades at a premium valuation of 12.94X forward P/S versus the industry average of 4.89X. items.title: Salesforce Stock Gains 34% in a Month: Time to Hold or Book Profits?
items.summary: Salesforce shares surged 34% in one month following strong Q2 FY2027 results showing stabilized double-digit revenue growth of 10.8% YoY and accelerating cRPO growth of 14%. Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5 billion with 240% YoY growth, positioning the company as an AI and enterprise data platform beyond traditional CRM. Despite the sharp rally, the stock trades at a reasonable 16.30x forward P/E, below sector averages and major competitors, suggesting room for upside. However, risks include potential pressure on per-user subscription models from AI agents and slower enterprise IT spending amid economic uncertainty.

items.title: Billionaire David Tepper Just Bought These 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That Wall Street Thinks Could Soar by 50% or More
items.summary: Billionaire David Tepper's hedge fund Appaloosa Management added SpaceX and CoreWeave to its portfolio in Q2, betting on their AI growth potential. items.title: Walmart Has Gone Practically Nowhere, While Target Is Up 68%. But Only 1 of These Dividend Kings Is a Buy in September.
items.summary: Target has surged 68% year-to-date while Walmart declined 4%, but the article argues Target is the better buy in September. Despite Target's recent momentum under new CEO Michael Fiddleke and positive comparable sales growth, Walmart remains a recession-resilient juggernaut with superior long-term performance. Target trades at a lower P/E ratio (17x vs 39x) and offers a higher dividend yield (2.8% vs 0.9%), while Walmart has demonstrated more consistent revenue growth and operational excellence over decades.

items.title: Nvidia, Palantir, and Meta Platforms Are Rattling Wall Street With This $18.6 Billion Warning

While insider selling can be attributed to tax obligations, the lack of insider buying raises concerns about potential AI bubble risks, as historical patterns show investors often overestimate adoption rates of breakthrough technologies.

items.summary: Bank of America demonstrates strong capacity for shareholder returns through robust earnings generation, healthy CET1 capital ratios, and disciplined balance-sheet management. items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed securities class action lawsuits against Intuit Inc. (INTU) and Rackspace Technology Inc. (RXT). The Intuit lawsuit alleges the company made false statements about its positioning in generative AI and Mailchimp's turnaround, concealing competitive pressures and growth failures. Investors with losses exceeding $100K are encouraged to join before the September 8, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline.

items.title: Schedule update: Stryker to participate in the 2026 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference

items.title: EQPT DEADLINE: ROSEN, RECOGNIZED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages EquipmentShare.com Inc Investors with Losses in Excess of $100K to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - EQPT
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying investors in EquipmentShare.com Inc (EQPT) and Rackspace Technology, Inc. (RXT) about ongoing securities class action lawsuits. EquipmentShare investors who purchased securities during the January-June 2026 period are being urged to act before the September 21, 2026 lead plaintiff deadline. The lawsuit alleges that EquipmentShare made materially false statements and failed to disclose undisclosed related party transactions and misleading financial statements. Similar allegations are being pursued against Rackspace Technology with a deadline in September 2026.

items.title: Broadcom (AVGO) Stock Is Down After Q3 Earnings: Is It Too Soon to Buy the Dip?
items.summary: Broadcom delivered exceptional Q3 results with 85% revenue growth and AI semiconductor revenue skyrocketing 221% to $16.7 billion. Despite beating expectations, AVGO stock fell nearly 3% due to Q4 guidance slightly missing some Wall Street forecasts. The stock is down 15% over the past month and trades at 34X forward earnings, making it more attractive but still vulnerable to high market expectations.

items.title: EQPT Investor Alert - EquipmentShare.com Stockholders with Large Losses Should Contact Robbins LLP for Information About the Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A securities class action has been filed against EquipmentShare.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: EQPT) for allegedly making false and misleading statements regarding undisclosed related-party transactions with entities owned or controlled by co-founders. Following a June 24, 2026 report by Umibōzu Research alleging $77+ million in undisclosed payments to founder-affiliated entities, EQPT stock declined over 34.5% from its $24.50 IPO price. Investors who purchased securities between January 23 and June 23, 2026 may be eligible to participate in the class action.

items.title: Jensen Huang Said This Word Exactly 1 Time During Nvidia's Earnings Call, and That Was Enough to Put Artificial Intelligence (AI) Bubble Fears to Rest
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's single use of the word 'visibility' during earnings signals the company's unprecedented insight into AI infrastructure demand across land, power, and supply chains. With top hyperscalers expected to spend $800 billion on capex in 2026 and $1.3 trillion in 2027, Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance and strategic equity stakes in networking and optical companies position it as the architect of AI factories rather than just a chip vendor, suggesting secular demand rather than a bubble.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Retain Cencora Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Cencora's U.S. Healthcare Solutions business demonstrated accelerating momentum with 5% revenue growth and 16% operating income growth in Q3, driven by specialty strength and OneOncology's performance. However, the company faces headwinds from manufacturer list-price reductions, the pending MWI divestiture expected to create a $150 million earnings impact, and regulatory uncertainty around 340B and ASP rules. GLP-1 growth and international operations provide diversification opportunities.

items.title: ROSEN, TOP-RANKED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Hims & Hers Health, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - HIMS
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit on behalf of Hims & Hers Health, Inc. investors for the period between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Hims made materially false and misleading statements regarding consumer health data sharing with third-party advertisers, premature prescription charges despite promised consultations, and undisclosed regulatory scrutiny and potential penalties. Investors who purchased securities during the class period may be eligible for compensation.

items.title: Don't Overlook These 2 AI-Driven Tech Stocks After Earnings: CIEN, NTAP
items.summary: Ciena and NetApp delivered impressive earnings results and raised guidance, capitalizing on AI infrastructure demand. Ciena's optical networking equipment saw 82% YoY cloud provider revenue growth with a raised FY2026 guidance to $6.42B (35% growth). NetApp posted record results with 30% YoY revenue growth to $2.02B and significantly raised FY2027 guidance to $7.98-$8.23B. Both stocks hold Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) ratings.

items.title: Physical AI Infrastructure Market to Reach $327.21 Billion by 2035 as Robotics and Autonomous Systems Accelerate Global Demand | Research by SNS Insider
items.summary: The global Physical AI Infrastructure Market is projected to grow from $14.20 billion in 2025 to $327.21 billion by 2035, with a CAGR of 36.91%. Growth is driven by deployment of AI systems in robotics, autonomous vehicles, smart factories, and edge computing. North America leads with 37% market share, while Asia-Pacific shows the fastest growth at 38.56% CAGR. Compute infrastructure and cloud deployment models dominate, with industrial automation and humanoid robotics as key applications.

items.title: ROSEN, SKILLED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Innventure, Inc. Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - INV
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a class action lawsuit against Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding Accelsius Holdings LLC's transformative deal with DarkNX, which was unlikely to materialize, and that revenue and cash flow targets for 2026 were overstated. Investors who wish to serve as lead plaintiff must file by October 27, 2026.

items.title: XTI AEROSPACE INVESTOR ALERT: Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C. Announces that a Class Action Lawsuit Has Been Filed Against XTI Aerospace, Inc. and Encourages Investors to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against XTI Aerospace, Inc. in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities and made materially false and misleading statements about the company's business operations and prospects during the period of April 15, 2026 to August 17, 2026. Investors who purchased XTI securities during this period and suffered losses are encouraged to contact the law firm.

items.title: HIMS Investor Alert: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP Encourages HIMS Investors with Losses to Contact the Firm
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (HIMS) for allegedly making material misstatements about its privacy practices. The FTC accused HIMS of sharing customers' medical information with third-party advertisers including Meta and Snap, and charging consumers for prescriptions immediately despite promising consultation with medical providers. The stock declined 14.73% on the news. Investors who purchased HIMS securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026 can seek lead plaintiff status by November 2, 2026.

items.title: Realty Income's Industrial Expansion: Can it Lift Long-Term Returns?
items.summary: Realty Income (O) is significantly expanding its industrial real estate portfolio, allocating about 75% of Q2 U.S. investments to warehouses and logistics. Industrial assets now represent 65% of global investments with stronger rent escalators (2-3.5% annually) and a 105.8% rent recapture rate. The company raised 2026 AFFO guidance to $4.44-$4.45 per share, with Q2 AFFO per share rising 3.8% to $1.09, though net debt remains elevated at 5.4x EBITDAre.

items.title: Fewer Than 30 Companies in the S&P 500 Have Raised Their Dividend for 50 Straight Years. This Financial Stock Is One of Them.
items.summary: S&P Global is highlighted as one of fewer than 30 S&P 500 companies that have raised dividends for 50+ consecutive years, achieving 54 years of increases. The company has delivered over 15% annualized returns over three decades, outperforming the S&P 500's 10.4%. Despite earlier concerns about AI disruption and disappointing Q4 results, S&P Global's dominant 50% market share in credit ratings, asset-light business model with 54% operating margins, and recent earnings guidance raise make it an attractive buy at current valuations of 26.4x earnings.

items.title: Securities Fraud Investigation Into Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) Continues – Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz
items.summary: A securities fraud investigation into Alphabet Inc. has been initiated following reports that Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model is months behind schedule. The company's stock fell 4.4% on July 16, 2026 after Bloomberg reported disappointing training results. Further declines of up to 7% occurred on July 23 after Alphabet announced a significant increase in capital expenditures to $195-205 billion for 2026, negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion, and expected margin pressure from reliance on third-party capacity.

items.title: AMP vs. PS: Which Stock Should Value Investors Buy Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two Financial - Investment Management stocks, Ameriprise Financial Services (AMP) emerges as the superior value option for investors. AMP holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with an improving earnings outlook and a Value grade of A, supported by a forward P/E of 12.21 and PEG ratio of 1.01. In contrast, Pershing Square (PS) has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) and Value grade of F, with a significantly higher forward P/E of 65.50 and PEG ratio of 3.75, making it less attractive to value investors.

items.title: Steris (STE) Down 2.1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: STERIS reported strong Q1 fiscal 2027 results with adjusted EPS of $2.59 (up 10.7% YoY) beating estimates by 1.97%, driven by higher volume, pricing, and productivity across all segments. However, revenues of $1.49 billion missed consensus by 0.83%. The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 guidance for 7-8% revenue growth and $11.10-$11.30 adjusted EPS. Despite solid earnings, shares have underperformed the S&P 500 by 2.1% since the report.

items.title: Figma, Inc. (FIG) Up 5.2% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Figma reported Q2 2026 earnings that beat expectations with $370.1M in revenue (48% YoY growth) and non-GAAP EPS of 8 cents. The company's AI monetization strategy is gaining momentum with over 80% of high-value customers consuming AI credits weekly. However, post-earnings estimates have shifted downward by 6.86%, and the stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with an F VGM Score, suggesting in-line returns ahead.

items.title: CVS Health (CVS) Up 1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: CVS Health reported strong Q2 2026 results with adjusted EPS of $2.58 (up 42.5% YoY) and revenues of $106.10 billion (up 7.3%), beating consensus estimates. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for earnings and revenues. However, estimates have trended downward over the past month with a -6.08% consensus shift, and the stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with expectations for in-line returns.

items.title: Charles River (CRL) Up 10.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Charles River Laboratories (CRL) shares have gained 10.5% since its Q2 2026 earnings report, outperforming the S&P 500. The company beat earnings estimates with non-GAAP EPS of $3.02 and raised its 2026 guidance, though revenues declined 2.7% year-over-year. However, estimates have been trending downward since the earnings release, and the stock carries weak VGM scores despite maintaining a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: Cencora (COR) Up 3.8% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Cencora reported Q3 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $4.48, beating consensus estimates by 2.5%, with 12% year-over-year earnings growth. Revenue rose 5.1% to $84.76 billion but slightly missed expectations. The company raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.75-$17.95 and increased operating income growth outlook to 13-14%. However, post-earnings estimates have trended downward, and the stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Kraft Heinz (KHC) Up 1.8% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Kraft Heinz beat Q2 2026 earnings estimates with adjusted EPS of 56 cents versus consensus of 53 cents, but organic sales fell 1.3% year-over-year. The company raised its 2026 organic sales guidance to a decline of 0.5-2% from prior guidance of 1.5-3.5%, though adjusted operating income guidance worsened to a 16-18% decline. Estimates have trended downward since the earnings release, and the stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with an expected in-line return.

items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Guided for 70% Revenue Growth in Fiscal 2028, Far Above the 44% Wall Street Expected, as Amazon Agreed to Buy 2 Million Nvidia GPUs. Is the Growth Forecast Believable?
items.summary: Nvidia provided a rare two-year revenue guidance of 70% year-over-year growth for fiscal 2028, significantly exceeding Wall Street's 44% expectation. The forecast is supported by Amazon's commitment to purchase 2 million GPUs and the rollout of Nvidia's new Vera Rubin architecture. Despite being a dominant market player, Nvidia has demonstrated accelerating growth, with 106% revenue increase in fiscal 2027 Q2, suggesting the ambitious target is achievable.

items.title: Why Sandisk Stock Rallied Today
items.summary: Sandisk stock surged 8.35% following Nvidia's $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, an open-source AI platform with 18 million users. The rally reflects investor confidence that Nvidia's expanded AI capabilities will drive demand for Sandisk's NAND flash memory chips, which are critical components in AI data centers. Dell's recent comments about memory constraints further supporting the outlook for memory chip demand.

items.title: EMCOR Rises 21% Year to Date: Should Investors Buy the Stock Now?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) has gained 21.2% year-to-date, outperforming its industry peers. The company benefits from strong demand across data centers, industrial, and construction markets, with Electrical Construction revenues up 24% and Mechanical Construction up 31% in Q2 2026. Record RPOs of $17.14 billion (up 44% YoY) and raised 2026 guidance to $20-$20.5 billion in revenue provide strong growth visibility. However, EME trades at a premium valuation with a forward P/E of 20.7 compared to industry peers.

items.title: Ciena Outlines Strong 2027 Outlook: What's Fueling the Momentum?
items.summary: Ciena Corporation reported Q3 revenue growth of 37% and adjusted EPS surge of 215%, driven by strong AI network spending. The company's backlog exceeded $10 billion with most demand for 2027, and it projects at least 30% revenue growth in fiscal 2027. Competitors Corning and Viavi Solutions are also benefiting from AI infrastructure and data center investments.

items.title: Is Marvell Technology a Millionaire-Maker Stock?
items.summary: Marvell Technology has delivered extraordinary returns (180% this year, 230% over 12 months) driven by its AI infrastructure business, but the article argues it is unlikely to be a millionaire-maker stock from current levels. With 79% of revenue from data centers and strong custom silicon growth targets, Marvell has solid fundamentals. However, high expectations are already priced in, it faces intense competition from Broadcom and others, and customer concentration creates volatility risk. The stock is recommended as a quality satellite position rather than a wealth-building core holding.

items.title: Every Hyperscaler Raised Capex Again. These 3 Boring Industrials Get Paid No Matter Who Wins the AI Race.
items.summary: Major tech companies (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) are significantly increasing capital expenditures for AI infrastructure. Rather than betting on which tech company will succeed, investors can gain exposure to the AI boom through industrial companies that supply essential infrastructure—power generation, electrical systems, and cooling hardware—regardless of which tech platform dominates.

items.title: Marc Benioff's $25 Billion Bet Against the "SaaSpocalypse" Earlier This Year Is Now Paying Off for Salesforce Investors, and It's Not Too Late to Join
items.summary: Salesforce's stock has surged 38% since March after CEO Marc Benioff's aggressive $25 billion accelerated share buyback during the AI-driven software sector sell-off. Q2 earnings revealed strong performance with AI-related revenue growing 210% year-over-year to nearly $4 billion, and a new partnership with Anthropic introducing Claudeforce. Despite the rally, the stock trades at just 16x earnings, suggesting potential for further upside as the company demonstrates it's an AI beneficiary rather than victim.

items.title: Baker Hughes Awarded Offshore Production Enhancement and Stimulation Services Contract by bp
items.summary: Baker Hughes has secured a significant multi-year contract from bp to provide offshore stimulation services across bp's UK North Sea operations. The agreement includes deployment of Baker Hughes' StimFORCE™ modular stimulation package on a dedicated vessel to support new well development and enhanced recovery from mature fields, leveraging a UK operating base and local supply chain.

items.title: OpenAI's Greg Brockman Says He Thinks Astra Might Be AGI. Here's Why That Matters for the Whole AI Trade.
items.summary: OpenAI announced its GPT-6 Astra model as a potential milestone toward artificial general intelligence (AGI), with President Greg Brockman calling it a 'generational leap.' However, the company's claims conflict with CEO Sam Altman's previous statements dismissing AGI as a 'marketing term.' Investors should remain cautious about AGI claims, especially as OpenAI prepares for an IPO.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Has 63% of Berkshire's $360 Billion Portfolio Concentrated in 5 Superstar Stocks
items.summary: Greg Abel, who took over as Berkshire Hathaway's CEO on December 31, maintains Warren Buffett's investment philosophy of concentrating assets in best ideas. As of August 28, 63% ($226 billion) of Berkshire's $360 billion portfolio is concentrated in five stocks. Tech stocks now comprise over 30% of the portfolio, driven by significant positions in Apple and Alphabet. Abel has tripled Berkshire's Alphabet position and added $17 billion in Q2. Meanwhile, Berkshire has been reducing its Bank of America stake for eight consecutive quarters due to valuation concerns.

items.title: PepsiCo vs. Coca-Cola: Which Stock Has the Edge?
items.summary: Coca-Cola (KO) demonstrates stronger fundamental performance compared to PepsiCo (PEP), with better volume trends, margin expansion, and higher earnings growth expectations. While PEP trades at a discount valuation, KO's superior operating metrics and 27% YTD outperformance justify its premium valuation, earning it a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) versus PEP's Rank #3 (Hold).

items.title: Nvidia’s $12.93 Billion Hugging Face Deal Expands Jensen Huang's AI Platform Beyond Chips
items.summary: Nvidia announced its acquisition of Hugging Face for $12.93 billion on September 3, 2026. The deal gives Nvidia control of a major open-source AI platform used by 18 million developers and 200,000 companies. While Nvidia pledges the platform will remain open and hardware-agnostic, the acquisition strategically positions Nvidia to influence AI software development decisions and potentially drive demand for its chips, despite the steep valuation relative to Hugging Face's $150 million annual revenue.

items.title: AI Infrastructure Demand Remains Red-Hot: HPE, AVGO, DELL Deliver
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Broadcom, and Dell Technologies all reported strong quarterly earnings driven by AI infrastructure demand. HPE posted record revenue of $12.2B with 34% YoY growth and raised FY26-27 guidance. Broadcom delivered $29.6B revenue (86% YoY growth) with AI semiconductor revenue surging 221% YoY. Dell achieved record $47B revenue (58% YoY growth) with a massive $95B AI server backlog. All three companies provided upbeat forward guidance, though market reactions were mixed as expectations remain sky-high.

items.title: BioNTech vs. Moderna: Which Is the Better Cancer Vaccine Stock to Buy Now?
items.summary: BioNTech and Moderna, both mRNA vaccine pioneers during the pandemic, are now pivoting to cancer vaccines as COVID revenue declines. Moderna is favored due to stronger recent clinical progress, including positive phase 3 results for its personalized cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and FDA approval for mFLUSIVA flu vaccine. While BioNTech has a deep pipeline including pumitamig, it has yet to deliver comparable phase 3 wins. Moderna's $61.2 billion market cap reflects investor confidence in its near-term commercialization prospects versus BioNTech's $26 billion valuation.

items.title: GPGI, Inc. Investors Have Until September 14th to Seek Lead Plaintiff Role with Bragar Eagel & Squire, P.C.
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against GPGI, Inc. in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York on behalf of investors who purchased GPGI Class A common stock between November 3, 2025 and May 6, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that defendants made materially false and misleading statements regarding the Husky acquisition, including overstating its value, misrepresenting revenue and EBITDA targets, and prioritizing fee generation over shareholder value creation. Investors have until September 14, 2026 to apply for lead plaintiff status.

items.title: Lululemon (LULU) Q2 Earnings Top Estimates
items.summary: Lululemon reported Q2 2026 earnings of $2.06 per share, beating consensus estimates of $1.79 by 15.08%, but revenues of $2.42 billion missed expectations by 2.07%. The stock has declined 42.2% year-to-date, significantly underperforming the S&P 500's 12% gain. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, the stock is expected to perform in line with the market. Management commentary will be crucial for determining future price movement.

items.title: Cencora Raises 2026 EPS Outlook as Specialty Businesses Strengthen
items.summary: Cencora (COR) raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.75-$17.95 following stronger-than-expected third-quarter results. The company's U.S. segment profit grew 15.9% driven by specialty sales and GLP-1 demand, while international operating income rose 20.8%. However, headwinds from lower-margin GLP-1 products, manufacturer price reductions, and higher financing costs tempered upside. The stock maintains a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Could Dell Be the Next Magnificent Seven Stock?
items.summary: Dell Technologies has transformed from a mature PC company into a primary beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout, reporting 58% revenue growth and 203% earnings surge. With a $95 billion AI server backlog and raised fiscal 2027 guidance, Dell is growing at rates comparable to younger tech giants, though it still lacks the market cap and margins of Magnificent Seven members. HPE's similarly strong results confirm the broader AI infrastructure cycle remains robust.

items.title: Greg Abel Bought $39.4 Billion of Stocks in 6 Months, Up From the $7.1 Billion Berkshire Purchased a Year Earlier Under Warren Buffett
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway shifted to net stock buying in Q2 2026 under CEO Greg Abel, purchasing $39.4 billion in equities during the first half of the year compared to $7.1 billion a year earlier. The company's most notable addition was Alphabet, making it the third-largest portfolio position. Despite a frothy market with elevated valuations, Abel is playing offense while managing $365.5 billion in cash and Treasuries awaiting deployment.

items.title: VEEV Raises FY27 Outlook as Vault CRM and AI Momentum Accelerate Fast
items.summary: Veeva Systems raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $3.682-$3.687B (implying ~15% growth), driven by strong Vault CRM adoption with commitments from 12 of top 20 biopharma firms and 180+ live customers. The company's Falcon AI product has five early adopters, though execution remains a key near-term priority. While profitability is maintained with a 44% operating margin, newer initiatives like CRM migrations and AI monetization still require sustained execution.

items.title: The Market Just Told You Which Layer Of AI Biology It Is Paying For
items.summary: Recent earnings in life sciences technology reveal that the market is rewarding companies with proprietary data and systems of record over those selling software or AI models alone. Veeva Systems beat expectations with strong AI product adoption, while Certara missed on modest software growth and Recursion Pharmaceuticals fell short on revenue expectations. MindWalk Holdings, which owns curated biological data infrastructure, is positioned to benefit from this trend with its HYFT Technology and newly launched ReefIQ platform, though it remains unprofitable with modest recurring revenue.

items.title: Why Palo Alto Networks Stock Jumped 15% In August Before Falling This Week
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks stock surged 15% in August driven by strong demand for cybersecurity solutions amid AI threats, but fell over 10% this week after reporting Q4 earnings with disappointing fiscal 2027 guidance of 23-24% revenue growth. The stock trades at a premium P/S ratio of 22x, requiring investors to believe in sustained 20%+ growth and significant margin expansion to justify current valuations.

items.title: Old Dominion Unveils Solid LTL Unit Performance for August
items.summary: Old Dominion Freight Line (ODFL) reported 12.4% year-over-year revenue per day growth in August 2026, driven by increased LTL revenue per hundredweight, despite a 0.9% decline in tons per day. Quarter-to-date LTL revenue per hundredweight rose 11.3% (4.8% excluding fuel surcharges). CEO Marty Freeman expressed confidence in the company's strategic positioning and capacity to capture profitable market share.

items.summary: XTI Aerospace, Inc. (XTIA) Shareholders Who Lost Money Have Opportunity to Lead Securities Fraud Lawsuit    Morningstar

items.title: I'm Calling It: Bloom Energy's Revenue Guidance Will Keep Surprising Wall Street Through Year-End
items.summary: Bloom Energy, a fuel cell manufacturer, has raised its full-year revenue guidance to $3.9-$4.2 billion (up from $3.4-$3.8 billion) driven by surging demand for AI data center power solutions. With Q2 revenue reaching $1.0 billion and expanding partnerships with Oracle and MiTAC, the company is well-positioned to continue delivering positive surprises through year-end as AI infrastructure investments remain robust.

items.title: Stock Market Midday, Sept. 3: Stocks Rally as Treasury Yields Fall, Broadcom Falls Despite Earnings Beat
items.summary: U.S. stock markets rallied on September 3, 2026, as Treasury yields fell and the probability of a September rate hike decreased. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled a preference for holding rates steady unless inflation surprises emerge. The S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq all gained over 1%, with industrials and financial services leading. Notable movers included Snowflake surging 20% on strong earnings, while Broadcom declined despite beating expectations. Nvidia gained on news of acquiring AI platform Hugging Face.

items.title: Equinix, NVIDIA & Together AI Accelerate Enterprise AI Inference
items.summary: Equinix has partnered with NVIDIA and Together AI to launch Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference platform for enterprises. The solution combines NVIDIA's Enterprise Reference Architectures, Together AI's inference capabilities, and Equinix's global infrastructure to enable faster, more cost-efficient AI deployment across multiple geographies. The platform will support metro-edge inference, open-source models, and sovereign AI requirements, with availability expected in Q1 2027.

items.title: Does Moderna's mRNA Flu Shot Face a New Challenge From GSK?
items.summary: Moderna secured FDA approval for mFlusiva, the first mRNA-based seasonal flu vaccine, establishing a foothold in the multibillion-dollar flu vaccine market. However, GSK announced plans to advance its own mRNA flu vaccine into phase III trials, which targets two viral proteins (HA and NA) and showed superior immune responses in phase II studies. While GSK's vaccine is still years away from market approval, it could pose a competitive challenge to Moderna's mFlusiva, which currently targets only HA like traditional flu vaccines.

items.title: Is COHR Stock a Buy as AI Growth Meets Premium Valuation and Risk?
items.summary: Coherent Corp. is projected to deliver strong fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 50.1% and earnings growth of 67.2%, driven by AI-optics demand. However, the stock trades at a premium 26.5X forward earnings with rising capital expenditures and weakening operating cash flow, creating execution risks. While earnings estimates are rising favorably, valuation and cash-flow pressures present concerns for investors.

items.title: YUMC or CMG: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two retail restaurant stocks, Yum China Holdings (YUMC) emerges as the better value option for investors. YUMC has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook, a forward P/E of 15.16, and a Value grade of A. In contrast, Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold), a forward P/E of 33.63, and a Value grade of F, making it significantly more expensive on traditional valuation metrics.

items.title: TransDigm (TDG) Down 8.1% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
items.summary: TransDigm Group reported Q3 fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of $10.87 per share, beating estimates by 5.6%, with sales rising 23% to $2.74 billion. Despite strong earnings and raised fiscal 2026 guidance, the stock has declined 8.1% since the earnings report. The company faces margin pressure from increased operating expenses and interest costs, though management remains optimistic with upward estimate revisions and a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

items.title: Spotify (SPOT) Up 16% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: Spotify reported Q2 2026 earnings with 300 million premium subscribers and 777 million MAUs, beating guidance on user metrics. However, EPS missed consensus estimates, and subsequent estimate revisions have trended downward by 12.06%. The stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating despite strong growth fundamentals, suggesting in-line returns ahead.

items.title: Airbnb vs. Spotify Technology: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Airbnb and Spotify Technology as investment options for 2026. Both companies have achieved profitability with similar leverage ratios (0.3x debt-to-equity), but differ significantly in margins and valuations. Airbnb generated $12.2B in revenue with a 20.5% net margin and $4.6B in free cash flow, while Spotify achieved $20.1B in revenue with a 12.9% net margin and $3.4B in free cash flow. The author recommends Airbnb due to its asset-light marketplace model, stronger profitability, capital efficiency, and more resilient growth potential, despite both facing competitive and regulatory challenges.

items.title: BE Investors Have Opportunity to Lead Bloom Energy Corporation Securities Fraud Lawsuit with SBS Law
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bloom Energy Corporation for alleged securities violations. The company is accused of making false and misleading statements regarding its sourcing of scandium, which was actually sourced from China through middlemen while the company understated its reliance on Chinese scandium. The class period runs from February 27, 2025 to July 8, 2026, with a deadline of September 28, 2026 for investors to participate.

items.title: NTAP Q1 Earnings & Revenues Top Estimates on AI and All-Flash Strength
items.summary: NetApp delivered record Q1 fiscal 2027 results with EPS up 66.5% to $2.58 and revenues climbing 29.9% to $2.03 billion, driven by strong AI spending and all-flash array sales reaching $1.31 billion. The company raised full-year guidance to $7.975-$8.225 billion in revenues with EPS of $9.73-$10.03, reflecting 17% and 22% growth respectively.

items.title: CIEN Q3 Earnings Beat on AI-Led Cloud Demand, Top Line Climbs 37% Y/Y
items.summary: Ciena Corporation reported strong Q3 fiscal 2026 results with adjusted earnings of $2.11 per share (215% YoY growth) and revenues of $1.67 billion (37% YoY growth), driven by AI-led cloud demand. Cloud provider revenues jumped 82% YoY and represented 53% of total sales. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to $6.42 billion and projects at least 30% revenue growth for fiscal 2027.

items.title: Deadline Approaching: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (HIMS) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact Law Offices of Howard G. Smith
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. following an FTC lawsuit alleging the telehealth provider shared consumers' sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms and engaged in deceptive billing practices. The stock declined 14.73% on the news. Investors who purchased HIMS securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026 have until November 2, 2026 to file a lead plaintiff motion.

items.title: 75% of Nvidia's $63 Billion Investment Portfolio Has Been Put to Work in Just 2 Game-Changing AI Stocks
items.summary: Nvidia has deployed 75% of its $63.4 billion investment portfolio into two major positions: a $30 billion stake in Intel (acquired for $5 billion in December 2025) and a $21 billion stake in SpaceX (via xAI investment converted to SpaceX shares after its June 2026 IPO). While the Intel investment appears secure with strong collaboration potential, the SpaceX position carries significant risk due to the company's negative free cash flow of $16 billion in Q2 2026 and ongoing losses despite its premium valuation.

items.title: A Once-in-a-Lifetime Investment Opportunity: The 3 Best Stocks to Take Advantage of the AI Build-Out
items.summary: The article recommends three stocks positioned to benefit from the AI build-out: Alphabet, leveraging Google Cloud's 82% YoY revenue growth; Nvidia, the world's largest company by market cap with expected 70% revenue growth; and Micron Technology, capitalizing on surging memory chip demand with projected 85% revenue growth in fiscal 2027.

items.title: Not Prime. Not Delivery. This Business Holds the Key to Amazon's Future.
items.summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is positioned as the primary growth driver for Amazon's future investment potential. Despite representing only 21% of sales, AWS generated 60% of operating income in Q2 with a 39.3% operating margin, compared to North American commerce's 7.8%. AWS grew 37% in Q2 while investing heavily in AI infrastructure, making it increasingly central to Amazon's profitability and margin expansion.

items.title: Tim Cook's Legacy at Apple Will Be Defined by This Nearly $879 Billion Investment, Not AI
items.summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on September 1, 2026, handing leadership to John Ternus. While Cook's tenure is often associated with iPhone innovation and Apple Intelligence, his true legacy is defined by nearly $879 billion in share buybacks since 2013. These aggressive repurchases significantly boosted earnings per share and stock performance, with Apple shares rising over 2,700% during his tenure. The buyback program accelerated after 2018 following the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, and is expected to continue under new leadership.

items.title: Opinion: Google's Latest Antitrust Ruling Is a Big Win for Alphabet Investors
items.summary: A federal judge rejected the DOJ's request to force Google to sell parts of its ad-tech business, allowing Alphabet to keep its powerful advertising engine intact. This decision mirrors a similar ruling one year ago that preceded a 16% stock jump. The ruling is significant as Alphabet's $81.63 billion advertising revenue is critical for funding its massive AI infrastructure investments.

items.title: 3 Millionaire-Maker Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks to Buy Now
items.summary: The article highlights three AI infrastructure stocks—Astera Labs, Credo Technology, and Vertiv—that address critical bottlenecks in AI data center scaling. Astera Labs specializes in connectivity solutions with 93% YoY revenue growth and a $6.5B Amazon warrant agreement. Credo Technology manufactures active electrical cables with 272% YoY growth but faces customer concentration risks. Vertiv dominates power and cooling systems with a $15B backlog and strong positioning in liquid cooling demand.

items.title: Vertiv Just Made an Up to $2.6 Billion Bet to Solve AI Data Centers' Biggest Bottleneck
items.summary: Vertiv is acquiring Utility Innovations for up to $2.6 billion to address the power supply bottleneck in AI data centers. The deal extends Vertiv's capabilities across the full power value chain from grid to chip, including microgrid solutions and on-site generation, enabling faster time-to-power for data center developers.

items.title: Where Will SoundHound AI Stock Be in 1 Year?
items.summary: SoundHound AI, trading near its 52-week low of $7, is predicted to rise approximately 25% over the next year. The company has experienced significant revenue growth from under $50 million to an expected $237 million this year, driven by expansion beyond automotive into restaurants, hospitality, and customer service. The pending acquisition of LivePerson could push combined 2027 revenue to $350-400 million, potentially justifying higher valuations if the company continues to perform well.

items.title: התראה על מועד אחרון לתביעה ייצוגית נגד MVST: רוזן, משרד עורכי דין מוערך, קורא למשקיעי Microvast Holdings, Inc. שספגו הפסדים העולים על 100,000 דולר, לשכור ייצוג משפטי לקראת המועד האחרון החשוב בתביעה ייצוגית בניירות ערך – MVST
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces class action securities lawsuits against Microvast Holdings, Inc. (MVST) and GPGI, Inc. (formerly CompoSecure, Inc.). The MVST lawsuit alleges defendants made false statements regarding profitability targets, manufacturing expansion capabilities, and vehicle launch timelines. Investors who suffered losses exceeding $100,000 during the relevant periods are encouraged to seek legal representation before the September 21, 2026 deadline for MVST and September 14, 2026 for GPGI.

items.title: התראה על מועד אחרון לתביעה ייצוגית נגד GPGI, CMPO: רוזן, משרד עורכי דין לליטיגציה, קורא למשקיעי GPGI, Inc. f/k/a CompoSecure, Inc. שספגו הפסדים העולים על 100,000 דולר, לשכור ייצוג משפטי לקראת המועד האחרון החשוב ב- 14 בספטמבר בתביעה ייצוגית בניירות ערך – GPGI, CMPO
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm announces September 14, 2026 deadline for investors to join a securities class action lawsuit against GPGI, Inc. f/k/a CompoSecure, Inc. The lawsuit alleges that defendants made false statements regarding the valuation of Husky acquisition, inflated revenue projections, and prioritized generating fees for insiders over shareholder value creation.

items.title: EquipmentShare.com Shareholder Alert: ClaimsFiler Reminds Investors With Losses In Excess Of $100,000 Of Lead Plaintiff Deadline In Class Action Lawsuit Against EquipmentShare.com Inc. - EQPT
items.summary: EquipmentShare.com Inc. (EQPT) faces a securities class action lawsuit alleging the company failed to disclose material information regarding undisclosed related party transactions and misleading financial statements in connection with its January 2026 IPO. Investors with losses exceeding $100,000 have until September 21, 2026 to file lead plaintiff applications.

items.title: BE DEADLINE: ROSEN, GLOBAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Bloom Energy Corporation Investors with Losses in Excess of $100K to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BE
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is soliciting investors who purchased securities of Bloom Energy Corporation (BE) between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026 to join a class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that Bloom Energy made materially false and misleading statements regarding its reliance on scandium sourced from China through intermediaries, which was not properly disclosed to investors. The lead plaintiff deadline is September 28, 2026. Similar class action notices are being issued for PROCEPT BioRobotics Corporation (PRCT) and Hertz Global Holdings, Inc. (HTZ).

items.title: HTZ IMPORTANT DEADLINE: ROSEN, GLOBAL INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages Hertz Global Holdings, Inc. Investors with Losses in Excess of $100K to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - HTZ
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying investors in Hertz Global Holdings (HTZ), PROCEPT BioRobotics (PRCT), and Bloom Energy (BE) about securities class action lawsuits. The firm is seeking lead plaintiffs with losses exceeding $100K, with a September 22, 2026 deadline. The Hertz lawsuit alleges defendants made false statements about liquidity and market conditions, leading to a dilutive capital raise that harmed shareholders.

items.title: BABA ALERT: Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA) Investors Urged to Contact Hagens Berman
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited, alleging the company misrepresented and failed to disclose its ties to China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), which classifies it as a Chinese military company under the NDAA. Additionally, Alibaba allegedly conducted fraudulent 'distillation attacks' against Anthropic's Claude AI models using fake accounts. The stock declined following these revelations in June 2026, and investors who suffered losses between June 26, 2025, and June 24, 2026, are urged to contact the law firm by October 5, 2026.

items.title: Pentair plc (PNR) Notice of October 2, 2026 Application Deadline for Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit against Pentair plc has been expanded to cover an earlier period (March 11, 2025 – July 14, 2026). The lawsuit alleges the company made materially false statements about its financial health and channel inventory, particularly in its Pool segment. On July 14, 2026, Pentair shocked investors with a massive revenue miss ($930M vs. $1.14B forecast), revealed $170M in inventory destocking impacts, slashed full-year guidance, and announced an abrupt CFO departure. The stock plummeted 15% the following day.

items.title: REGN 12-DAY DEADLINE ALERT: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors Alerted to September 14, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline in Class Action Lawsuit
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals for allegedly making false and misleading statements about its Phase 3 clinical trial of Fianlimab for melanoma treatment. The company reportedly failed to disclose that preliminary statistical assumptions were flawed and the primary endpoint was unlikely to be achieved. After initially expressing confidence in the trial, Regeneron altered the trial protocol in November 2025 without timely disclosure and ultimately announced on May 15, 2026 that the trial failed to reach statistical significance, resulting in an $11 billion market cap loss.

items.title: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) Reports Q1 Loss, Beats Revenue Estimates
items.summary: C3.ai reported a quarterly loss of $0.2 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.26 loss, with a 23.08% earnings surprise. However, revenues declined year-over-year to $52.38 million. The stock has lost 23.3% since the beginning of the year and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

items.title: Deadline Alert: GoDaddy Inc. (GDDY) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP About Securities Fraud Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against GoDaddy Inc. alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements between September 3, 2025 and February 24, 2026. The lawsuit claims GoDaddy failed to disclose that its high-intent customer strategy was failing and that promotional discounts on .com domains were negatively impacting bookings and revenue. The stock fell 14.28% on February 25, 2026 following the disclosure of disappointing fourth quarter results.

items.title: How Dell's AI Server Boom is Driving Hockey-Stick Growth
items.summary: Dell Technologies reported Q2 EPS of $7.04, beating consensus estimates by 41.65%, driven by strong AI server demand. The company set multiple revenue records and is on track to double revenue and EPS by 2028. Management projects AI will comprise 75% of data center demand by 2030, with inference workloads expected to grow significantly.

items.title: Deadline Alert: Intuit Inc. (INTU) Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged To Contact Glancy Prongay Wolke & Rotter LLP About Securities Fraud Lawsuit
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Intuit Inc. alleging the company made materially false statements about its competitive advantages and business strength. The lawsuit was triggered after Intuit announced a 17% workforce reduction and reported weak TurboTax revenue growth of only 7% (vs. 8% consensus), causing the stock to plunge 20% on May 21, 2026. Investors who purchased INTU securities between February 25, 2025 and June 1, 2026 can file a lead plaintiff motion by September 8, 2026.

items.title: BABA Stock Drop: Robbins LLP Reminds Investors They May Be Eligible to Lead the Class Action Against Alibaba Group Holding Limited
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited for allegedly failing to disclose that it was considered a Chinese military company and at risk from U.S. crackdowns on such entities. The stock dropped significantly following the U.S. Department of Defense's inclusion of Alibaba on a Chinese military companies list in June 2026, and further declined after Bloomberg reported Alibaba of illicitly accessing AI models. Investors who purchased BABA between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026 may be eligible to participate.

items.title: DELL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong AI Demand Aids Revenue Growth
items.summary: Dell Technologies reported Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings of $7.04 per share, beating estimates by 41.65%, with revenues surging 58% to $46.97 billion driven by record AI server orders of $60.9 billion. The company raised fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $192 billion and expects $74 billion in AI server revenues, with ISG revenues jumping 89% year-over-year to $31.78 billion.

items.title: Sandisk Stock: Buy, Sell, or Hold?
items.summary: Sandisk stock has quintupled year-to-date and appears poised for further gains as Samsung's announcement of multiyear memory chip deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet through 2031 intensifies the memory shortage. Sandisk is growing faster than Samsung (372% vs 130% YoY revenue growth) and securing similar long-term contracts, providing revenue visibility and pricing power. With a 77% net profit margin and only a 20 P/E ratio, the company is well-positioned to capitalize on sustained AI-driven demand for memory chips.

items.title: Reasons Why Zebra Technologies Stock Should Be in Your Portfolio
items.summary: Zebra Technologies (ZBRA) reported Q2 sales growth of 25.9% in Connected Frontline and 13.5% in Asset Visibility segments. The company raised its 2026 revenue growth guidance to 14-16% and increased free cash flow outlook to over $1 billion. ZBRA completed the acquisition of Elo Touch Solutions and returned $568 million to shareholders through buybacks, supported by strong product demand across its businesses.

items.title: Kaplan Fox & Kilsheimer LLP Alerts Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (NYSE: HIMS) Investors to a Securities Class Action Deadline on November 2, 2026
items.summary: A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. for the period between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026. The FTC sued the company for failing to disclose immediate prescription charges, making subscription cancellations difficult, and sharing consumer health information with third-party advertising platforms like Meta and Snap. The stock fell 14.73% following the FTC allegations. The lead plaintiff deadline is November 2, 2026.

items.title: Why The Trade Desk Stock Rallied Today
items.summary: The Trade Desk stock surged 4.9% after the FTC and 22 states filed suit against Amazon for allegedly using deceptive ad pricing practices, including undisclosed surcharges. This legal action highlights The Trade Desk's competitive advantage through transparent pricing and could help the company recapture market share from competitors with closed ecosystems.

items.title: Salesforce: Its Biggest AI Threat Just Became Its Partner
items.summary: Salesforce partnered with Anthropic to integrate Claude as the default AI reasoning engine across its products including Agentforce and Slack. The deal addresses investor concerns about AI disrupting Salesforce's business model while creating a powerful upsell opportunity, as AI features are exclusive to premium subscriptions. The stock surged 23% on the announcement, and Q2 results showed 11% revenue growth and 240% annualized growth for Agentforce to $1.5 billion.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding its Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo study. The complaint claims the study's preliminary statistical assumptions were flawed, the treatment arm showed no meaningful clinical differentiation from standard therapies, and the study was unlikely to achieve statistical significance on its primary endpoint. The class period covers purchases between August 1, 2025 and May 15, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Alibaba Group Holding Limited Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Alibaba Group Holding Limited alleging securities fraud. The lawsuit claims that Alibaba made materially false and misleading statements regarding its business operations and prospects, specifically related to alleged control by China's MIIT (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology) and undisclosed risks of AI model distillation attacks. Investors who purchased Alibaba securities between June 26, 2025 and June 24, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 5, 2026.

items.title: AMG vs. BLK: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) and BlackRock (BLK) are compared as potential value investments in the Financial - Investment Management sector. AMG holds a stronger Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) versus BLK's #3 (Hold), with superior valuation metrics including a lower forward P/E ratio of 9.83 compared to BLK's 20.19, and a better Value grade of B versus D. AMG is identified as the more attractive value opportunity based on improving earnings outlook and fundamental metrics.

items.title: Sysco's Fiscal 2027 Outlook Puts AI Cost Savings in the Spotlight
items.summary: Sysco Corporation projects fiscal 2027 sales growth of 6-7% to ~$90B and adjusted EPS growth of 9-11%, driven by AI-enabled productivity initiatives expected to deliver $100M in cost savings. However, the company's outlook depends on stable restaurant traffic and modest inflation, with execution risk around converting planned savings into sustained margin expansion while continuing infrastructure investments.

items.title: Quanta's Net Income Nearly Doubles: Can Profit Growth Stay Hot?
items.summary: Quanta Services (PWR) reported exceptional Q2 2026 results with net income nearly doubling to $451.4 million and revenues climbing 41.1% to $9.56 billion. The Electric segment led growth with 43.6% revenue increase and 62.5% operating income surge. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for net income to $1.74-$1.82 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $4.09-$4.21 billion, supported by strong infrastructure demand and recent acquisitions.

items.title: Dell's $95 Billion Backlog Answers the AI Question
items.summary: Dell Technologies posted record quarterly revenue of $46.97 billion (58% YoY growth) with non-GAAP EPS of $7.04 (203% YoY growth), significantly beating consensus estimates. The company booked a record $60.9 billion in AI server orders and exited with a $95 billion backlog. Dell raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $192 billion from $167 billion, implying 69% growth. Gross margins expanded 260 basis points to 20.9%, disproving concerns that AI servers carry structurally lower margins. Growth extended beyond AI servers, with traditional servers up 122% and storage up 26%.

items.title: Berkshire's Biggest New Position Came From Warren Buffett, Not From Greg Abel
items.summary: Warren Buffett, now president of the board after Greg Abel became CEO of Berkshire Hathaway in early 2026, initiated a massive $8.5 billion investment in Alphabet during the second quarter. The article suggests a division of responsibilities is emerging, with Abel managing Berkshire's sprawling business portfolio while Buffett continues overseeing investment decisions, potentially setting a precedent for future leadership transitions.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of Innventure, Inc. Investors
items.summary: The Portnoy Law Firm has announced a class action lawsuit on behalf of Innventure, Inc. investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Innventure and its officers misled investors about a purported 300MW data center deal with DarkNX. After a May 28, 2026 report questioned the deal's legitimacy, and following Innventure's August 13, 2026 disclosure that the DarkNX project was removed from internal bookings, the stock price fell 55% to $1.62 per share.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of XTI Aerospace, Inc. Investors
items.summary: The Portnoy Law Firm has announced a class action lawsuit on behalf of XTI Aerospace investors who purchased securities between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities requiring Board review, raising doubts about the effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures, which prevented timely filing of earnings reports. Investors have until October 27, 2026 to file a lead plaintiff motion.

items.title: Is AI-Powered Infrastructure Turning MasTec Into a Bigger Winner?
items.summary: MasTec (MTZ) reported strong Q2 2026 results with 23% revenue growth to $4.4B and 49% EPS surge to $2.22. The company raised full-year guidance and achieved a record $21.4B backlog, driven by AI data center infrastructure, renewable energy, and power generation demand. The company is compared favorably to peers EMCOR and Dycom in capturing AI infrastructure opportunities, though MTZ stock trades at a premium valuation with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Nvidia Is Still Retail Investors' Most-Held Stock on Robinhood, but a New Trillion-Dollar Stock Has Entered the Top 10
items.summary: Nvidia remains the most-held stock among retail investors on Robinhood, driven by AI enthusiasm. SpaceX has recently entered Robinhood's top 10 as a trillion-dollar company, but the article warns that its accelerated insider share unlock schedule and low public float percentage could disadvantage retail investors.

items.title: Company News for Sep 2, 2026
items.summary: Medtronic and MiniMed Group posted better-than-expected first-quarter revenues, driving their shares up 1.5% and 10.7% respectively. However, NIO Inc. fell 4% after missing revenue estimates. Apple gained 2.6% following the appointment of John Ternus as new CEO.

items.title: Here's What $1,000 Invested in Berkshire Hathaway the Day Greg Abel Became CEO Is Worth Now
items.summary: Since Greg Abel took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway at the end of 2025, the stock has been essentially flat, with a $1,000 investment worth only $1,005 today. This marks a stark contrast to Warren Buffett's legacy of 19.7% average annual returns. Despite solid Q2 earnings and a strong cash position of $365.5 billion, Berkshire is on track for its worst performance in over a decade.

items.summary: The Trade Desk's stock plummeted 24% in August following disappointing Q2 earnings that showed just 3% revenue growth and missed profit estimates. CEO Jeff Green lacks a clear turnaround strategy, raising concerns about the company's long-term relevance.

items.title: Broadcom Reports Wednesday. Its Profit Is Growing Nearly 4 Times as Fast as Its Revenue.
items.summary: Broadcom's profit growth (127%) is significantly outpacing revenue growth (32%) due to disciplined cost management, with operating expenses rising only 6% while revenue jumped 48% in fiscal Q2. The company's fiscal Q3 earnings report on September 2 will test whether this cost discipline holds as revenue is expected to reach $29.4 billion. However, at a P/E ratio of 60x, the stock's valuation depends heavily on maintaining this profit growth trajectory, which could face pressure from AI product mix headwinds and eventual expense scaling.

items.title: 3 Lesser Discussed Stocks That Offer Meaningful AI Exposure
items.summary: While NVIDIA dominates AI discussions, investors can gain exposure to AI trends through alternative companies. items.title: Stock Market Today, Sept. 1: Intel Falls on Chip Stock Pressure
items.summary: Intel closed down 0.60% at $88.97 on September 1, 2026, as higher Treasury yields and inflation concerns pressured semiconductor stocks broadly. The decline was driven by macro factors rather than company-specific issues, with peers like AMD and Qualcomm also falling. Intel's recent $20 billion equity offering and progress in reducing foundry business losses provide some optimism, though near-term volatility is expected as investors assess whether Intel can maintain its position in the AI market.

items.title: Portnoy Law Firm Announces Class Action on Behalf of EquipmentShare.com Investors
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against EquipmentShare.com (NASDAQ: EQPT) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between January 23, 2026 and June 23, 2026. The complaint alleges the company made false statements and failed to disclose undisclosed related-party transactions benefiting co-founders through entities like EZ Equipment Zone, Bevel Financial, and Armada Fleet Management. Following a June 24, 2026 Umibōzu Research report detailing these allegations, the stock fell over 6% that day and nearly 12% the following day.

items.title: Aon's $17 Billion USI Deal: A Costly Bet on Middle-Market Growth
items.summary: Aon is acquiring USI Insurance Services from KKR for $17 billion to expand its U.S. middle-market insurance brokerage footprint. The deal, expected to close in Q4 2026, will add specialty insurance access and analytics capabilities while generating approximately $395 million in annual EBITDA synergies. EPS accretion is projected for 2028, though the transaction requires significant debt financing and suspension of share repurchases in the near term.

items.title: Nvidia Sells the Brains of the AI Boom. Something Else Is Selling the Muscle -- and It's Not on Wall Street's Radar.
items.summary: While Nvidia dominates AI chip sales, an overlooked opportunity exists in 800-volt power distribution equipment for data centers. This technology offers ~10% cost savings over conventional power supplies and is being developed by companies like Vertiv and Nvidia. Though the transition could take years given the industry's $700 billion annual AI infrastructure spending, this emerging sector presents significant long-term potential.

items.title: Amazon Doesn't Pay a Dividend and Constantly Dilutes Shareholders. Here's Why I'd Still Buy and Hold It Forever.
items.summary: The article argues that Amazon is a compelling long-term buy despite not paying dividends and diluting shareholders through equity compensation. The author contends that Amazon's powerful Prime ecosystem (valued at $1,430 annually vs. $139 cost), expanding rural logistics network, and strategic AI investments through AWS and partnerships with Anthropic create an unassailable competitive moat. Rather than returning cash to shareholders via dividends, Amazon reinvests profits into infrastructure and innovation, positioning it as a compounding growth machine.

items.title: Vertiv Plunges 20% in Three Months: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Vertiv shares fell 20% in three months due to project delays and supply-chain issues, but the company reported strong Q2 results with 24% sales growth and 22.6% adjusted operating margin. Benefiting from robust AI infrastructure demand, Vertiv expects Q3 sales of $3.65B-$3.85B and adjusted EPS of $1.77-$1.83. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (20.94X Price/Book) and faces stiff competition, earning a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Eni Builds Uruguay Offshore Presence Through New Exploration Deals
items.summary: Eni has signed agreements to expand its presence in Uruguay's offshore exploration sector. The Italian energy company will operate the OFF-5 block with MIWEN (YPF subsidiary) holding 50%, and will acquire a 40% stake in the neighboring OFF-6 block operated by APA Corporation. Eni will fund a significant portion of an initial exploration well scheduled for 2027. These moves strengthen Eni's position in Latin America and diversify its upstream operations.

items.title: I've Been Wrong About Philip Morris International Stock for 5 Years. Here's Why I'm Finally Changing My Mind.
items.summary: The author reverses his 5-year bearish stance on Philip Morris International after the company successfully pivoted from declining cigarettes to higher-margin smoke-free products. Smoke-free products now represent 42% of revenue (up from 24% in 2020), with strong growth in IQOS heated tobacco and ZYN nicotine pouches. Q2 results beat expectations with 10.4% revenue growth and 15.2% EPS growth. However, at current valuations near $192, the stock is no longer considered cheap despite the improved business fundamentals.

items.title: Amazon vs. Shopify: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Amazon and Shopify as investment options for 2026. Amazon dominates with $716.9B in revenue and a 10.8% net margin but faces regulatory scrutiny and plans $200B in capex spending for AI infrastructure. Shopify, growing at 30.1% annually with zero debt and $2B in free cash flow, is positioned as the higher-growth, lower-risk alternative. The author recommends Shopify for investors seeking high rewards with relatively low risk.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Intuit Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Intuit Inc. alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims Intuit made false statements about its competitive advantages and business strength, while concealing significant losses in its TurboTax business due to competitive and pricing pressures. The class period covers August 22, 2025 to May 20, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of September 8, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges EquipmentShare.com Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm

(NASDAQ: EQPT) alleging that the company made materially false and misleading statements regarding undisclosed related-party transactions with co-founders and misrepresented its financial condition during its IPO and subsequent trading period from January 23, 2026 to June 23, 2026. Investors who suffered losses have until September 21, 2026 to request lead plaintiff status.

items.title: JSAIY vs. WMT: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of J. Sainsbury PLC (JSAIY) and Walmart (WMT) as value investment options reveals that JSAIY is the superior choice. JSAIY has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 14.50 and Value grade of A, while WMT has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 36.51 and Value grade of D. JSAIY's lower valuation metrics and improving earnings outlook make it more attractive for value investors.

items.title: Sundar Pichai Says Alphabet's AI Overviews Now Reach 2.5 Billion Monthly Users as Ad Revenue Hit $82 Billion. Does That Scale Justify Spending Up to $205 Billion on AI Infrastructure This Year?
items.summary: Alphabet is investing up to $205 billion in AI infrastructure in 2026, building on $91 billion spent in 2025. The company's AI initiatives have reached 2.5 billion monthly users through Google Search's AI Overviews and generated $82 billion in ad revenue. Google Cloud revenue surged 82% year-over-year to $25 billion in Q2 2026. Despite taking on $114 billion in debt, Alphabet maintains positive free cash flow of $53 billion over the trailing 12 months, positioning it competitively ahead of peers like Amazon and Meta in the AI infrastructure race.

items.title: Broadcom Set to Report Q3 Earnings: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Broadcom is expected to report Q3 fiscal 2026 results on September 2 with revenues of ~$29.4 billion (84% YoY growth) and AI semiconductor revenues accelerating to ~$16 billion (200%+ YoY growth). However, gross margin pressure from lower-margin AI semiconductors and stretched valuation present headwinds. The stock has underperformed peers despite strong AI momentum with major customers including Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta.

items.title: Netflix Is Down 46% From Its High. Is This a Once-in-a-Lifetime Buying Opportunity Before the Stock Goes Parabolic?
items.summary: Netflix stock has fallen 46% from its all-time high amid revenue growth deceleration, but the company maintains strong profitability with a 33.4% operating margin and is executing on key initiatives including ad-tier expansion (250M+ users), live programming (NFL, WWE), and a $25 billion share buyback program. While not a 'once-in-a-lifetime' opportunity, the stock at 19-22x 2026 earnings represents reasonable valuation for a maturing business with solid long-term fundamentals.

items.title: Nebius vs. CoreWeave: Which Is the Better Artificial Intelligence (AI) Infrastructure Stock to Buy Right Now
items.summary: Nebius and CoreWeave are neocloud infrastructure companies benefiting from surging AI data center demand, with the market expected to grow at a 58% CAGR through 2031. Nebius has outperformed with 146% gains in 2026 and improving profitability, while CoreWeave trades cheaper but faces higher losses despite a stronger revenue backlog of $104 billion. Both stocks offer long-term growth potential depending on investor risk profile.

items.title: Lowe's Cuts 2026 Outlook as DIY Pressure Tests Its Growth Engines
items.summary: Lowe's beat Q2 earnings expectations with $4.40 EPS but missed revenue forecasts and significantly lowered fiscal 2026 guidance to flat comparable sales and $12.25 EPS. While Pro, Online, and Home Services segments showed strength with 15.7% online sales growth, weak DIY demand, housing pressures, and margin headwinds from fuel, transportation, and competitive pricing drove the cautious outlook reset.

items.title: Stryker to Acquire ZuriMED to Expand Its Shoulder Care Portfolio
items.summary: Stryker announced a definitive agreement to acquire ZuriMED, developer of the FiberLocker System for rotator cuff augmentation. The acquisition aims to strengthen Stryker's shoulder portfolio and expand its rotator cuff repair capabilities in sports medicine and arthroplasty. Despite the strategic move, SYK shares fell 2.1% following the announcement, though the global rotator cuff repair market is projected to grow at 7.6% CAGR through 2033.

items.title: Is AIDR Emerging as CrowdStrike's Next Major Growth Engine?
items.summary: CrowdStrike's AI Detection and Response (AIDR) business nearly tripled its annual recurring revenue sequentially in Q2 fiscal 2027, driven by strong enterprise demand for AI security solutions. AIDR operates as a separate, incremental product using existing Falcon agents, with token-based pricing creating additional recurring and usage-based revenue opportunities. However, CrowdStrike trades at a premium valuation of 32.97x forward P/S versus the industry average of 18.51x, and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Construction Partners Expands Asphalt Operations With Oklahoma Deal
items.summary: Construction Partners, Inc. (ROAD) acquired Asphalt Express Enterprises, a liquid asphalt supply and hauling business in Ardmore, OK. Through its subsidiary Overland Corporation, ROAD gained a rail-served industrial site, trucks, and trailers. The company plans to develop the location into a liquid asphalt terminal to improve sourcing and transportation across Oklahoma and North Texas. However, ROAD shares declined 3.5% following the announcement.

items.title: Prediction: Amazon Could Be Worth This Much in 5 Years
items.summary: Amazon is expected to outperform the broader market over the next five years, driven by strong growth in its cloud computing segment (AWS) and AI investments. The article projects Amazon's stock could reach approximately $460 by 2031, representing a 12% annualized return, assuming 12% annual earnings growth and stable valuation multiples. Key growth drivers include AWS's 37% year-over-year revenue growth, internally developed AI chips improving margins, and productivity gains in e-commerce.

items.title: Buy 5 AI-Powered Momentum Stocks for September After a Strong August
items.summary: U.S. stock markets surged in August driven by renewed AI enthusiasm, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite advancing 2.6% and 3.9% respectively. Five AI infrastructure leaders—NVIDIA, Super Micro Computer, Semtech, SiTime, and Keysight Technologies—all holding Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings with momentum scores of A, are expected to maintain their upward trajectory. NVIDIA's data center revenue jumped 117% year-over-year to $89 billion, while Semtech projects 160% year-over-year data center growth in Q3.

items.title: Here's How Much You'd Have If You Invested $1000 in Synopsys a Decade Ago
items.summary: A $1,000 investment in Synopsys (SNPS) made in September 2016 would have grown to $7,414.24 by September 2026, representing a 641.42% gain—significantly outperforming the S&P 500's 254.05% return. The company benefits from recurring revenue, strong demand for chip design and AI-related tools, and the Ansys acquisition expansion, though elevated debt and execution risks remain concerns.

items.title: Nvidia Just Proved It Doesn't Need China Anymore
items.summary: Nvidia provided fiscal 2028 guidance forecasting 70% revenue growth, significantly exceeding Wall Street's 44% expectations. The company demonstrated it can achieve substantial growth without relying on China, where it now generates less than 1% of data center revenue. With a forward P/E of 23 and PEG ratio of 0.6, Nvidia appears undervalued despite its accelerating growth trajectory.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Started His Tenure With a Bang by Paring Down Bank of America and Making a Virtual Monopoly Berkshire's No. 3 Holding
items.summary: Greg Abel, who took over as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway on December 31, has made significant portfolio changes in his first year. He has systematically reduced Bank of America holdings over eight consecutive quarters (down 53% cumulatively) due to valuation concerns and interest rate sensitivity. Simultaneously, Abel has aggressively increased Alphabet (Google) holdings to $17 billion in Q2, making it Berkshire's third-largest position, driven by the company's dominant search market share and strong AI growth potential in Google Cloud.
