items.title: Li Lu, "the Chinese Warren Buffett," Has Invested 70% of Himalaya's Capital in Just 2 Stocks
items.summary: Li Lu's Himalaya Capital has concentrated 70% of its $3.7 billion portfolio into two stocks: Alphabet (48%) and PDD Holdings (22%). Alphabet is viewed as a strong long-term buy despite DOJ antitrust concerns and AI competition, while PDD Holdings trades at cheap valuations but faces headwinds from U.S.-China trade tensions and slowing Chinese economic growth.

items.title: Broadcom Has Seen Its Biggest Customer Drop a Key Chip Before. History Says What the Stock Did Next.
items.summary: Broadcom's stock fell ~5% on August 19 after Marvell announced an expanded custom chip agreement with Google, Broadcom's most important AI customer. However, historical precedent from Apple's 2023 design-away announcement suggests these transitions are slow and partial. After Apple dropped a Broadcom wireless chip, the company's revenue nearly doubled and stock gained over 500% as AI demand surged. The key difference this time is that Google's orders directly impact Broadcom's core AI business, making the concentration risk more significant at current valuations.

items.title: Walmart Just Posted Its Biggest One-Day Drop Since 2022. History Says What Its Big Drops Have Been Worth.
items.summary: Walmart stock fell 9.2% on August 20, 2026, despite raising its full-year outlook, due to decelerating comparable sales growth (2.6% vs. 4.6% year-over-year). Historical analysis shows the company's three larger drops over 15 years were followed by modest 6-14% gains within a year, though the current valuation at 37x earnings and slowing growth suggest caution rather than a bargain opportunity.

items.title: Berkshire CEO Greg Abel Is Sitting on Nearly $400 Billion in Cash. Here's How His Deal-Making Approach Differs From Warren Buffett's.
items.summary: Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway's new CEO, has inherited nearly $400 billion in cash and is signaling a shift from Warren Buffett's hands-off management style. Abel's acquisition of Taylor Morrison Home for $8.5 billion suggests he plans to integrate overlapping businesses into unified units, a more hands-on approach focused on operational synergies and bolt-on acquisitions rather than Buffett's strategy of buying companies and letting them operate independently.

items.title: Amazon's Free Cash Flow Went Negative by $7.6 Billion Even as Operating Cash Flow Rose 33%. Here's the Gap AI Capex Is Actually Creating.
items.summary: Amazon generated $161.4 billion in operating cash flow over the past 12 months (up 33% YoY) but spent $169 billion, resulting in negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion. The company's massive AI capital expenditure spending is driving this cash burn, forcing Amazon to raise $77 billion in long-term debt, which increased from $65.6 billion to $128.9 billion. Investors should look beyond earnings metrics and focus on the concerning cash flow and balance sheet implications of AI spending.

items.title: Applied Digital vs. TeraWulf: Which AI Data Center Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Applied Digital and TeraWulf are competing AI data center stocks benefiting from the AI boom. Applied Digital has more contracted power capacity (1.4 gigawatts vs. 839 megawatts), a larger pipeline (3 gigawatts vs. 2.1 gigawatts), higher revenue, and lower losses. Despite these advantages, both companies have similar market caps (~$7.8-7.9 billion), making Applied Digital the better value pick for investors.

items.title: AT&T's Dividend Costs the Company a Fixed Amount Every Quarter Regardless of Competitive Pressure From Starlink or Cable Rivals. Here's the Coverage Ratio That Actually Determines Whether It's Safe.
items.summary: AT&T maintains a sustainable 4.4% dividend yield despite competitive pressures from cable operators and Starlink. With a 36% trailing payout ratio and 45% cash dividend payout ratio, the company has ample coverage to support its ~$2 billion quarterly dividend. Share buybacks have actually strengthened the dividend's footing, reducing dividend outlays year-over-year despite competitive threats.

items.title: Cardinal Health's CFO Moved $9.9 Million of Stock. Here's What Long-Term Investors Should Know
items.summary: Cardinal Health's CFO Aaron Alt sold 42,000 shares worth $9.9 million on August 18, reducing his direct holdings to 20,495 shares. The sale occurred after the stock surged 57% over the past year. Despite the insider sale, the company maintains strong guidance with fiscal 2027 EPS projected at $12.40-$12.60 (13-15% growth), planned capital expenditures of $700 million, and at least $1 billion in share repurchases expected.

items.title: Cardinal Health's Medical Segment Boss Sold $8 Million in Stock. Here's What to Know
items.summary: Stephen M. Mason, CEO of Cardinal Health's GMPD Segment, sold 35,000 shares worth $8.3 million on August 18, reducing his direct holdings by 29%. While the stock has gained 57% over the past year, the Medical segment continues to face challenges with declining revenue and profit margins, with fiscal 2027 projections ranging from $200-220 million depending on geopolitical factors.

items.title: If Amazon Is a Top Growth Stock, Then Why Does It Trade at Just 21.3x Forward Earnings While the S&P 500 Trades at 20.4x? This Is the Only Answer I Can Think Of.
items.summary: Amazon trades at a modest 21.3x forward earnings despite strong growth, slightly above the S&P 500's 20.4x multiple. The company reported impressive Q2 results with 20% sales growth and AWS revenue up 37.5% year-over-year, driven by AI demand. The author attributes the relatively low valuation to market expectations that mega-cap companies face growth caps compared to smaller upstarts, despite Amazon's continued double-digit growth across e-commerce, cloud services, and emerging chip and satellite businesses.

items.title: Cardinal Health's Pharma Chief Sold 7,354 Shares and Still Grew Her Stake by 47%. Here's How That Happened
items.summary: Deborah Weitzman, CEO of Cardinal Health's PSS Segment, sold 7,354 shares for ~$1.7 million on August 18, 2026, but still increased her total stake by 47% after receiving performance units. Despite the sale, her direct holdings grew to 77,901 shares valued at $18.31 million. The Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions segment she leads showed strong performance with 6% revenue growth and 21% profit growth in Q4, with specialty business growing over 25% in fiscal 2026.

items.title: The CIO of Cardinal Health Parted With 11,650 Shares. Here's Whether It Matters for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Cardinal Health's CIO Michelle Greene sold 11,650 shares worth $2.7 million at a weighted average price of $235.72, reducing her direct stake by roughly 16%. While the sale follows strong stock appreciation, the article notes that Greene sold more aggressively than other executives like the CEO and legal officer. The transaction occurred amid the company's August award cycle and comes as Cardinal Health guides lower adjusted free cash flow for fiscal 2027 despite record capital expenditures in technology and automation.

items.title: Billionaire David Tepper Has 16% of His $7.5 Billion Appaloosa Portfolio in Amazon Stock. Is It Still a Buy?
items.summary: David Tepper's Appaloosa Management increased its Amazon position by 15.8% in Q2, with Amazon now representing 16% of the $7.5 billion portfolio. The move reflects a pivot from AI infrastructure plays to hyperscaler stocks. While AWS showed strong 37% revenue growth driven by AI infrastructure demand, Amazon trades at a 22x forward earnings multiple. The bull case hinges on continued AI-driven growth, though an AI bubble burst could significantly impact the stock.

items.title: Synaptics' Top Lawyer Sold Stock as a $7 Billion Merger Moves Toward Closing. Here's What to Know
items.summary: Synaptics' Chief Legal Officer Lisa Bodensteiner sold 20,274 shares worth $2.2 million on August 17-18, 2026. The sale included 14,218 shares withheld for taxes on vested equity awards and 6,056 shares sold under a pre-established Rule 10b5-1 trading plan from September 2025. The transaction occurred as Synaptics moves toward closing its $7 billion all-stock acquisition by onsemi, expected in mid-2027. Bodensteiner's position grew overall after acquiring 41,734 shares through vesting two days prior.

items.title: Is It Too Late to Buy Sandisk After Its 568% Run?
items.summary: Sandisk has surged 568% in 2026, becoming the top-performing Nasdaq-100 stock, driven by massive AI infrastructure spending on memory solutions. The company benefits from $93.9 billion in locked-in long-term supply contracts, a strategic Kioxia joint venture, and aggressive share buybacks. Despite the rally, Sandisk trades at a forward P/E of 7—a steep discount to semiconductor peers—suggesting the stock remains undervalued given strong AI tailwinds and unprecedented demand visibility.

items.title: Ross Stores Grew Comparable Sales 10%. TJX Grew 4%. Only One Stock Went Up.
items.summary: Ross Stores and TJX Companies reported earnings for the same 13-week period with vastly different market reactions. Despite TJX posting 4% comparable sales growth and raising full-year guidance, its stock fell 4%. Ross Stores, with 10% comparable sales growth driven by increased customer traffic, saw its stock jump 4%. The key difference lies in forward guidance: Ross expects 6-7% comparable sales growth in Q3, while TJX projects only 2-3%, with its flagship Marmaxx division nearly flat.

items.title: Does Greg Abel Know Something Wall Street Doesn't? New Berkshire Hathaway CEO Doubles Down On a Legacy Department Store Stock With a 3.3% Dividend Yield
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Greg Abel has more than doubled the company's position in Macy's during Q2, despite the stock being a legacy department store. Macy's has executed a successful turnaround strategy called 'A Bold New Chapter' since 2024, achieving its best comparable sales growth in four years, with Bloomingdale's posting record growth. The stock has risen 78% over the past year and offers a 3.3% dividend yield, trading at a low valuation with strong free cash flow generation.

items.title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Dropped a 9-Word Warning: "Margin Debt Is the Highest It Has Ever Been." Should Investors Be Worried?
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that margin debt has reached all-time highs while asset prices remain elevated, creating potential systemic risk. Record margin debt combined with modest stock price declines could trigger widespread margin calls, forcing investors to sell stocks and potentially creating a downward spiral that breaks the bull market. Dimon also highlighted concerns about geopolitical tensions, inflation, and fiscal deficits.

items.title: Insider Sells Over 17,000 Shares of Utility Stock, Valued at Nearly $700,000
items.summary: Jesus Soto Jr., EVP and COO of CenterPoint Energy, sold 17,075 shares worth $686,000 on August 11, 2026, through a non-discretionary transaction to cover tax withholding on vesting restricted stock units. Despite the sale, Soto retains 173,355 shares and over 146,000 RSUs vesting through 2029. CenterPoint Energy is positioned to benefit from data center growth in Texas but faces a $67 billion expansion plan that could lead to share dilution.

items.title: A Tempus AI Director Sold Stock Four Days Before a 24% Rally. Here's What to Know
items.summary: Nadja West, a director at Tempus AI, sold 3,000 shares for $161,700 on August 14 under a pre-established Rule 10b5-1 trading plan set up in May. Four days later, the stock rallied 24% following news that Moderna and Merck's cancer vaccine succeeded in late-stage trials. West retained 34,981 shares worth ~$1.8 million. The sale timing appears coincidental as it was scheduled months in advance, and the company reported strong Q2 results with 22% revenue growth and its first GAAP profit.

items.title: Is Tempus AI Stock a Buy After Its 75% Rally? Here's What to Know as the Firm's Legal Chief Files a Trade
items.summary: Tempus AI's Chief Legal Officer Andrew Polovin sold 30,075 shares worth $1.5 million in a non-discretionary transaction to cover tax withholding obligations from RSU vesting. The sale occurred during a 75% stock rally driven by positive results from a Moderna-Merck cancer vaccine trial validating Tempus's genomic sequencing technology. The company reported 22% revenue growth to $382.5 million last quarter and achieved its first GAAP profit, though it remains unprofitable on a TTM basis with -$254.4 million net income.

items.title: Tapestry's Top Lawyer Filed a Stock Transaction. Tariffs Are the Bigger Story
items.summary: Tapestry's Chief Legal Officer David E. Howard sold 4,884 shares worth $643,000 on August 19 to cover tax obligations from restricted stock unit vesting. The transaction is non-discretionary and not indicative of changed investment outlook. The article highlights that tariffs remain a significant concern for Tapestry heading into fiscal 2027, with CFO Scott Roe noting tariffs will provide modest benefits in H1 but become a headwind in H2.

items.title: UPS Fired Amazon. Was It The Smart Move?
items.summary: UPS's decision to reduce Amazon delivery volume by 50% aligns with its 'better, not bigger' strategy to focus on higher-margin business segments. However, the stock has declined 10.5% since the announcement due to margin concerns. While management raised earnings guidance, operating margins actually decreased, and fuel surcharges appear to be the primary driver of revenue growth rather than operational improvements.

items.title: Why Robinhood Markets Stock Popped Today
items.summary: Robinhood Markets stock surged 13.70% on Friday following optimism about cryptocurrency industry regulation. The Trump administration is pushing Congress to pass the Clarity Act, which would establish clearer crypto regulations and enable financial institutions to integrate digital assets more easily. CEO Vlad Tenev highlighted opportunities in tokenized stocks, which Robinhood already offers in 120+ countries but cannot yet provide in the U.S.
